expected: Holes found and closed without stopping working jobs
lesson: A watchdog must bound its own waits: the runner's join on a job's output was the one wait nothing watched. Judge activity by the job's own counters, not the machine's.
result: Holes: (1) a job that exits but leaves a background child holding its stdout kept the runner waiting until the child ended (measured: 25 s for a 25 s child; forever for a daemon) because the reader's join was unbounded, and heartbeats had already stopped, so the station hung silently to the 350-minute timeout. (2) stall activity used the whole machine's network bytes, so other runner traffic could mask a real hang. (3) a CPU-busy loop is never idle, so nothing ever flagged it. (4) a stall reached STATUS only as exit 124 'failed'. Fixes: bounded join (10 s grace), then SIGTERM and SIGKILL of the job's process group (a 600 s orphan stopped at 15 s, none left); the job's own /proc rchar+wchar decide activity, machine network only when unreadable; one ::warning when a run exceeds 3x its last successful duration and 30 minutes (never a stop); STATUS.json gains rattle_watch {elapsed, max_silent, stalled, overrun_warned, orphans_stopped} and stopped_by rattle_watch_stall. Attack on the fix: the report could carry the previous job's watch into a job that failed early (reset per job); the watch dict copy lost the report (shared now). 15 Rattle Watch tests.

(2) Expensive models must not do clerical work; scripts do, as in Papinian's prep.sh and render_producer.py. (3) An auto-review burst means a sandbox gap; fix the permission, do not pay a review per command. (4) Stop on measured spend per verified claim (3M units, 40 minutes), not on hours or on what agents report. (5) Every run needs a budget. Wired in jobs/carnot-coordinator/meter.py and jobs/savigny-supervisor/supervisor.py.
result: 910M input tokens, 881M (97%) of them cache re-reads, and 3.87M output. Very High coordinators took about 490M (54%) over about 3,000 tool calls averaging about 190k context (peak 447k), auto-review sessions about 227M (25%, 150 sessions), workers about 190M (21%). Per verified filed claim: lane I 5.9M usage units, lane II 9.1M, lane III 26.8M, lanes IV and V 16M each for 0. Papinian (Claude), same window: 63 filed for 297 USD, coordinator 17%, driving scripts.

expected: A gap in the record: lessons the project had not learned yet.
lesson: A lessons register stops nothing unless a gate enforces it at the decision point. jobs/augur-launch/augur.py refuses a wave unless: its objective is an outcome; its actions are Bentham's; it ramps from a 1-lane, 30-order stage 0 for any unmeasured configuration; every matching Kean warning is answered; it has a pre-mortem; and a reviewer of another model family or the owner signed its hash. The Savigny supervisor runs that check at startup. Replayed on the overnight plan, Augur refuses it for eight of the reasons it failed.
result: The lessons existed, and the coordinator cited most of them in the wave's own prompts. Carnot PROTOCOL (coordinators over half of past waves' cost); F-20261109-gutenberg-carnot (run the next wave as the measured lean-coordination arm); Bentham README (pre-1937 strata unmeasured); F-20261107-haloander-undecided-probe (0 of 30); Montfaucon 0 of 50. What failed was the structure: lessons were pull-only, the author approved his own plan, the objective drifted to using the allowance, a never-run configuration went straight to five lanes, and there was no forecast and only late, self-reported feedback. Outside the project the pattern is the same: GAO-02-195 found 23% of NASA managers had ever contributed to the agency's lessons system; Google SRE launch reviews and Flagger's metric-gated canaries are the established fixes.
tried: Checked what the project already knew before the overnight Codex wave launched (2026-11-09 21:45 ET), and why none of it stopped the wave. Researched how other fields keep known lessons from being missed.

Amender listings in a parent's status line are not evidence the amender is in force (P2). expected: Self-executing and amendment-only orders get an admissible NO basis under P2 (owner answer to A-20261106-pothier, 2026-11-09) and D-20261028-evidence-decides.
lesson: A classifier whose claim is a negative ('no continuing command anywhere') must fail closed: any command word not accounted for by a recognised form disqualifies. Adding wordings to a list does not fix a fail-open default. Blind reads on disjoint samples are cheap (about 0.7 USD each) and should gate any lead class before a lot is built on it; 95% lead precision still does not license sampled adoption.
result: 687 undecided orders get OWN_TEXT records (261 spent_on_issue, 426 amends_parent, 211 with an unidentified parent; 369 on an acceptable original; 321 had no NO basis before); Pothier agrees on 306 and holds 29 open. Blind precision (Sonnet 5.5, sealed labels): 85% and 84% on the first versions, 57 of 60 (95%, CI 86-99%) after the classifier was made fail-closed. Diagnosed: OWN_TEXT for EO 12178, 12378, 12379, 13013, 13552, 7621, 5739; EO 13116/13064 gain retyped TERMs. Review found a fail-open classifier (EO 8100's forest reservation passed) and false 'retained' sunsets; fixed; re-review approve with nits.

lesson: A lexical 'prints the number' test is a lead, never a legal fact: recording its miss as 'unnamed' and gating on it blocks correct NOs, and its hits need refusals for hyphenated state numbers, citation lists, years, list tails and governors. Non-official renderings (federalregister.gov) stay leads; holding the govinfo PDFs would make 1,002 orders' records citable.

Diagnosed: EO 8790 and 8649 (PLO texts) basis-eligible; EO 13354 and 14231 census windows; EO 13204's rescission rules leads only. The first version claimed 1,549 orders; review found the lexical number test attached state governors' orders, misprints and FR citations to the wrong EO (58 of 70 low-number FRDOC rows wrong) and let federalregister.gov renderings pass as a basis; fixed (5 known-wrong low-number rows remain, all leads); re-review approve.
